findings.summary: V12-F4-5 (the pinned-host internal candidate order) is registered as INFORMATIONAL, but its documented source (amendment record F4-R4 and architecture review AR-ADR022C3-05) is LOW, and the worker report's own stated rule says F4-R4 is LOW - a mis-severity and a self-contradiction in the worker evidence.
findings.detail: The task requires the eight bounded residuals to be evidence-based and correctly classified in the register, and the review delegation explicitly asks to flag any residual that is mis-severitied. The project convention is that an accepted item's severity is copied from its source finding: V12-F3-1 is LOW because its source SR-17.4-02 is LOW (docs/implementation/17.4/security-review.json:25-26). For F4, the documented severities are in the amendment record `docs/implementation/planning/v1.2-f4-clause-3-amendment.json` residual_limitations: F4-R1 MEDIUM, F4-R2 MEDIUM, F4-R3 LOW, F4-R4 LOW (lines 56-84). F4-R4's own source finding AR-ADR022C3-05 is also LOW (docs/reviews/architecture/adr-022-clause-3-conformance.json:68-80). The register nevertheless labels V12-F4-5 INFORMATIONAL in both current-state surfaces (docs/limitations/00-index.md:113 and docs/limitations/accepted.md:947), and the worker report's `interpretations[3].chosen` says 'V12-F4-5 ... INFORMATIONAL (ADR-029 F4-R4 ...)' (worker-report.json:106). The same interpretation's `basis` (worker-report.json:107) states the rule as 'the amendment record severities F4-R1/F4-R2 MEDIUM and F4-R3/F4-R4 LOW' - i.e. the worker itself records F4-R4 as LOW and then labels the item INFORMATIONAL. Every other one of the eight residuals maps correctly (V12-F4-1 MEDIUM<-F4-R1 MEDIUM, V12-F4-2 MEDIUM<-F4-R2 MEDIUM, V12-F4-3 LOW<-R-19.1-02 LOW, V12-F4-4 LOW<-F4-R3 LOW, V12-F4-6 INFORMATIONAL<-R-19.1-04 INFORMATIONAL, V12-F6-1 LOW<-19.3-F1 LOW, V12-F6-2 INFORMATIONAL<-source inspection), so this is a single isolated classification error, not a systemic one. Impact is documentation/register accuracy only: no behaviour, state, or test is affected, and the ID set, names, register placement, and evidence traces are otherwise correct. It is a required correction because the register is the task's primary deliverable and the item's severity is a carried classification field, and because the worker's evidence for it is internally inconsistent.
evidence: docs/implementation/17.4/security-review.json:25-26 + docs/limitations/accepted.md:789 (V12-F3-1 LOW copied from SR-17.4-02 LOW, the established convention)
findings.recommended_action: Re-label V12-F4-5 as LOW in docs/limitations/accepted.md:947 (title) and docs/limitations/00-index.md:113 (row), and correct the worker report's stated basis so the register severity agrees with the amendment record F4-R4 / AR-ADR022C3-05. No production, test, ADR, or state.json change is required.

findings.area: Register accuracy: V12-F4-4 precondition vs ADR-029 residual 3 wording
findings.summary: V12-F4-4 narrows ADR-029 residual 3's 'removing or making ineligible the boundary anchor' to 'removed or no longer a movie/episode candidate', but it discloses the service-ineligible distinction explicitly and matches the shipped implementation, so no change is required.
findings.detail: ADR-029 clause 4 / Consequences residual 3 says an anchor that 'was removed or became ineligible' resets the cursor. The shipped locate step matches the unique itemId, so an item that remains an enumerable Movie/Episode candidate but becomes service-ineligible is still located and the cursor does not reset; only removal or leaving the candidate enumeration resets. The accepted entry (docs/limitations/accepted.md:926-946) states this precondition and explains the distinction, and the same interpretation is independently recorded by the 19.2 test-quality review TQ-19.2-02 (docs/implementation/19.2/test-quality-review.json:19-29). The register is therefore more precise than the ADR wording rather than inaccurate, and the ID/title ('An unlocatable cursor anchor resets the run to the start') is correct. Recorded for audit only; no action required.
